title: EXPLORE SOFTWARE OR TOOL SUBSCRIPTION WITH CHATGPT
content:
A software or tool subscription works when customers continue paying because the tool continues providing useful access or functionality.

The business is not simply "build an app and charge monthly." A recurring payment creates a recurring expectation. The tool needs an ongoing reason to remain useful enough to keep.

START WITH THE REPEATED JOB
What does the customer need to do repeatedly? What problem returns often enough that ongoing access makes sense? A one-time problem wrapped in monthly billing is usually not a strong subscription concept.

ONGOING VALUE CAN TAKE DIFFERENT FORMS
The value might come from stored data, automation, monitoring, collaboration, continually updated information, repeated workflows, or another function that remains useful over time.

SOFTWARE ALSO CREATES ONGOING RESPONSIBILITY
Hosting, bugs, security, support, integrations, data handling, and maintenance may continue after launch. You do not need to solve the technical architecture in this guide, but you should notice whether you actually want a business with that kind of continuing responsibility.

COPY & PASTE INTO CHATGPT

Interview me about a software or tool subscription idea. Ask who the user is, what repeated job or problem they have, what they currently use, how often the problem occurs, what the tool would need to do, why ongoing access is more appropriate than a one-time product, and what level of technical maintenance or customer support I am willing to own.

Help me narrow to the smallest useful version worth investigating. Separate must-have functions from later features. Identify assumptions about customer demand, technical feasibility, integrations, hosting, security, privacy, support, pricing, and operating costs that require outside research or qualified expertise.

Do not claim that an idea is technically feasible or commercially validated just because it sounds plausible.

At the end give me:
- Intended user
- Repeated problem/job
- Core ongoing value
- Smallest useful version
- Why subscription rather than one-time purchase
- Ongoing operational responsibilities
- Major assumptions to verify
- Concise business-direction statement

WHERE TO GO NEXT
If the direction is clear, continue to PDF 46. If the ongoing value is primarily information rather than software functionality, compare PDF 34.
